title: The Rhythm Club jam sessions: Willie the Lion humbles Sedric; Autrey's own test
summary: At the Rhythm Club on 132nd Street dozens of players sat in and were booed off if weak; Sedric left in tears after Willie the Lion's put-down and came back ready, while Autrey says he was tested by Henderson.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Aw, he was a heck of a musician, damned good, and congenial cat, and he could play, and loved to play. Oh (laughs) Sedric told me -- tell about that man -- well, some years ago. He said when he first came to New York -- (laughs) -- well at that time, if you were in New York, I don't care what instrument you played, and you went into the Rhythm Club on certain days, when they had a -- any time a guy came in he thought it was good, he'd say okay (slam), I'm here.

There were (unintelligible) session. Now, this will be 50 drummers, 50 piano players, 50 clarinets, 50 trumpets, 50 anything, than the Rhythm Club, 132nd Street (unintelligible). That's what they did. Now, if you were good, if you

thought you were good, they would listen. That's up to you. And you'd better be doggone good, because them -- man, those cats'll blow you out. So the cats were playing. I don't care what the tune was, just ask you what'd you like? What tune do you want? Then they would play it, and you know.

"I Got Rhythm, Saint Louis Blues, Bugle Call Rag," whatever you name. I mean the standard tunes that they played, you know. All right. Turn the [PAUSE], be in there playing jam session, all and what not.
All at the Rhythm Club.

Yeah. Rhythm Club. I don't care how good you are, the guys would listen, and if you had something to offer they would applaud, and they would give it to you, and shake your hand, and whatnot. But if you couldn't play they'd -- Prffft -- they would boo you out of there. Right?
So that's what was happening. Now, who were we talking about?
Gene Sedric.

Gene Sedric. Sedric came up and while he was sitting there playing he was -- Willie the Lion was sitting there, ding-da-dingle ling, dingle linga linga, playing, you know, and Sedric say he'd sit there a while, and he looks, listens (laughs) so he take his bag out from under his arm, and lay it down, and Willie the Lion -- look -- Willie the Lion looks at him sitting there. If you can't play that
thing, don't take it out. You know, and kept on --
(Laughter.)
Ding-a-ling-a-ling-a-ling, (Laughter.)
: Willie the Lion, right?

Yeah, so the Lion -- so he's saying, he got mad. He said who the hell is this guy? Who is he to tell me that? Said he was very mad. Willie kept playing, said the guys were blowing. If you can't play it, don't take it out here, you know. That's the way they was, Willie the Lion was.
So he started crying, saying Ah, so he took this horn out, put it back in the bag and went on home.
(Laughter.)
: Really crying?

Yeah, that's what he told me. See, because he was -- he had hurt his feelings. So he went home (laughs) saying, and he said that so-and-so. Said he called him all kind of names, you know, and after he got home. So he practiced at home, got himself together, so he came back the next time. So when he came back the next time he felt ready and right. He didn't care who was out there, he took his horn out and started playing.
Well that's the way they did you. If you couldn't play, and you pulled your horn out, I mean you'll only make an ass of yourself, and you had to stay in there and get back
groove in the group, and get yourself together, and until you were ready.
What happened to you the first time you went to the Rhythm Club?

Well, when I -- (laughs) God damn! Thank God I was blowing. I was playing, but I never hung up on this thing like Sedric. I never had that, because well that happened downtown where I told you Pops Foster went in for me, stood up for me, and I went and played and everybody liked me, and I was a good guy. When I came uptown, and I went on -- another thing I was blowing, but I never really had to stretch until I went with Fletcher Henderson job in his house and took over the job as playing first trumpet, and he gave me all the first parts and moved me over in the first space.
That's why -- that was it, you know. That was my, you know, one of those things. I happened to have what was needed, and I kept going, and kept moving, you know.
